reasons.reader_question: The ending hands the reader a sharp question: will he touch her and take the cold, learning she lied right after saying 'Good. I'd hoped'?
reasons.change: Ila moves from in control on the ice to hurt by her own lie. Kunal's relief now rests on a falsehood the reader can see.
reasons.romance_movement: Her first lie breaks trust at its peak. The reason is new: fear that the truth would turn him back.
reasons.shown_chemistry: Shown through action: he walks her track blind, says 'You're looking at me.' 'Yes.', lifts the bowl from her lap, she spares him the ash smear.
reasons.character_logic: The lie is well motivated, since refusal is closed. But an exact measurer budgeting 'an hour' for a lie that would turn him round is a slip.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: The world rule bites in flesh, her compounding lies make the cost larger, and showing her hands will expose her.
reasons.prose: Concrete and clean, with no banned phrases or AI tells. Minor echoes: 'said it gently' twice, 'eyes on the fire' twice, 'very still/very quiet'.
reasons.continuity: Matches the bible's lie sizes, the fire rule, the hut (F515), the name trade (F462) and the letter in her coat lining before ch 20.

fixes: At 'She could keep them hidden for an hour', Ila misjudges the lie's size (irrational behaviour). She knows a lie is sized by how much the truth would change his choices, and this one would turn him round. Have her size it as middling, plan on a night of shaking, and say 'No' anyway. The choice becomes deliberate and costlier, and the later '*Middling*, she thought' becomes confirmation, not discovery.

At 'The cold began in her fingertips, as it always began. She had read about it.', the text contradicts itself. 'As it always began' implies she has felt lie-cold before, and 'read about it' clashes with hearing Meera's account. Cut both phrases. Open with the needle under the nails, then recall Meera's flat account and glove at the Garh Neshar drafting table, to match F576.

Fix the prose echoes. At the second 'He said it gently', in the 'Show me your hands' exchange, replace the tag with an action beat, such as him putting the pot's weight on one knee. Cut the second 'eyes on the fire' at 'He turned the bowl in his hands'. Change one of 'Kunal had gone very quiet' or 'Now he sat very still' to a concrete gesture.
reader_question: When Kunal sees her white hands, will he take her cold and learn that the 'No' he was so glad of was a lie?
new_facts_assessment: All four facts are useful and consistent. F699, Kunal closing the narrow-truth evasion, is the key device: it makes the lie costly instead of artificial. Keep F697 and F698, but F698 should say the drafting table, not 'the hall', to match F576. F696 needs S7 tracking as the draft notes. S7 should also retire F517 ('six days') and revisit F512, because this chapter, ch 13 and F525 all support 'more than two weeks'.
